SecuVidyra Academy

Ethical Hacking Foundations

For learners with networking and operating-system fundamentals.
12 weeks: 48 live hours + 48 guided practice hours
Outcome: demonstrate skills through lab evidence and an individual submission.

Proposed schedule. Dates, fees and mode to be confirmed.

Learning modules:

CEH preparation pathway

Independent foundation material supporting further CEH study.
Official training, exam eligibility and vouchers require separate confirmation.
No vendor endorsement or exam-pass guarantee.



Threats, weaknesses and controls

A threat can exploit a weakness.
A control reduces likelihood or impact.
Residual risk remains after controls.



Reconnaissance and privacy

Passive research gathers already available information.
Active discovery interacts with a target.
Collect only information needed for the approved objective.



Service discovery

Document approved address ranges.
Identify reachable services with agreed limits.
Correlate observations with the asset inventory.



Enumeration and exposure

Service responses can disclose roles or configuration.
Excessive detail can support later attacks.
Restrict unnecessary information and anonymous access.



Credential security

Prefer unique credentials and strong authentication.
Store passwords using appropriate salted password hashing.
Rate limits and monitoring reduce automated guessing.



Endpoint attack concepts

Privilege boundaries limit the impact of a compromised account.
Patching and application controls reduce attack paths.
Logs help investigate suspicious execution.



Malware and incident response

Malware may steal data, disrupt systems or maintain access.
Isolate affected assets through approved procedures.
Preserve evidence and communicate impact.



Network traffic and segmentation

Encrypted traffic protects content in transit.
Segmentation restricts reachable systems.
Packet metadata still supports troubleshooting and detection.



Social engineering defences

Verify unusual requests through a trusted channel.
Report suspected phishing without forwarding secrets.
Simulation needs consent, boundaries and support.



Wireless and mobile security

Use strong wireless authentication and managed updates.
Separate guest access from internal systems.
Review mobile permissions and device protections.



Cloud and shared responsibility

Provider and customer responsibilities differ by service.
Review identities, exposed storage and network rules.
Capture configuration evidence with approved access.



Cryptography in practice

Encryption protects confidentiality with keys.
Hashes help detect changes but need trusted comparison values.
Digital signatures support integrity and origin verification.



Web, APIs and secure design

Check identity and permissions at each boundary.
Treat input and uploaded files as untrusted.
Use security logs without exposing secrets.



Study method and exam integrity

Map learning gaps to the current vendor objectives.
Practise with legitimate questions and authorised labs.
Explain why each answer is correct.
Confirm eligibility directly before paying for an exam.



Capstone

Analyse a fictional organisation across endpoint, network, cloud and web risks.
Submit a threat-control map, evidence log and prioritised recommendations.
Present a five-minute incident-response tabletop.

Independent CEH preparation only. Not official EC-Council training. Exams, eligibility and vouchers are separate.

Academy completion certificate only. No employment guarantee.
